The course's main goal —
zero injuries,

callout_text:
practical
modules of
comprehensive

norm: SafetyHUB curriculum • Company safety standard

title: Electrical safety basics
subtitle: Electric current is invisible, odourless and acts instantly. The only protection is knowing the laws and strictly following the rules.
norm: PUE RK • Safety Rules for the operation of electrical installations

title: Electrical safety at work
bullets: • Work environment: electrical installations up to and above 1000 V, switchboard rooms, cable routes and switchgear.
• Nature of the hazard: electric current shows no outward signs of danger (no colour, smell or sound in normal operation).
• Human factor: loss of vigilance, getting used to danger and ignoring the rules cause over 80% of severe electrical injuries.
• Main rule: every electrical installation is considered live until proven otherwise and until earthing is in place.
callout_text:
Electric current
forgives no mistakes:
the lack of visible
danger dulls
your vigilance!
norm: PUE RK Chapter 1.1 • Electrical Installation Code

title: Effects of electric current on the human body
rows: Thermal
Severe tissue burns, vessel heating, boiling blood and lymph
Insulation, protective shields, arc-rated PPE
Electrolytic
Decomposition of body fluids, blood breakdown, chemical changes
De-energising, dielectric gloves and insulated tools
Mechanical (dynamic)
Torn muscles, tendons and blood vessels, fractures, dislocations
Automatic disconnection (RCD, fast-acting relays)
Biological
Muscle spasms, cardiac fibrillation, respiratory arrest
Equipotential bonding, TN neutral connection, earthing
bottom_banner: Severity depends on the size of the current, the exposure time and its path through the body.
norm: GOST 12.1.009-2017 • Cross-industry labour safety rules

title: 4 thresholds of alternating current (50 Hz)
steps:
Perceptible current:
slight tingling,
faint itch in the fingers.

Non-let-go current:
irresistible muscle spasms,
the hand cannot unclench.

Fibrillation current:
chaotic heart contractions,
circulatory arrest.

Lethal current:
instant heart paralysis,
the most severe thermal burns.
bottom_banner: A current of just 0.1 A (100 mA) for 1–2 seconds is fatal!
norm: GOST 12.1.038-82 • Maximum permissible current and voltage levels

title: Local electrical injuries and effects
bullets: • Electrical burns: contact current burns (current passing through tissue) and arc burns (arc temperature reaches 4000–6000 °C).
• Electrical marks: firm grey or yellowish spots of dead skin with sharp edges at the current entry and exit points.
• Skin metallisation: tiny splashes of molten metal driven into the epidermis by an electric arc.
• Electro-ophthalmia: inflammation of the cornea and conjunctiva from intense arc UV radiation (goggles or a face shield required).
callout_text:
Electric arc
temperature reaches
6000 °C —
working without a face
shield and arc suit
is deadly!
norm: Cross-industry first aid instruction

title: Current paths through the body (current loops)
bullets: • Danger of a current loop: set by the share of total current passing through vital organs — the heart, lungs and brain.
• “Hand — hand” loop: ~3.3% of the current passes through the heart. The most common workplace case when touching two phases.
• “Left hand — feet” loop: up to 4.0% of the current reaches the heart — the most critical, dangerous path!
• “Foot — foot” loop: step voltage current; ~0.4% passes through the heart, but falling to the ground turns it into “hands — feet”.
callout_text:
A fall in the current zone
instantly turns the loop
from “foot-foot”
to the deadly
“hands-feet”!
norm: PUE RK • Safety Rules

title: CRITICAL BAN: Dangerous approach distances
warning_title: ABSOLUTE BAN ON APPROACHING LIVE PARTS:
bullets: • Do not approach unguarded live parts closer than the set minimum distances (up to 1 kV — 0.6 m; 1–35 kV — 0.6 m; 110 kV — 1.0 m; 220 kV — 2.0 m).
• Do not work alone in electrical installations where the work permit requires a second person to be present.
• Do not touch live insulators and structures without basic electrical protective equipment.
• Do not continue work if there are signs of arcing, an unusual transformer hum or a smell of burning.
bottom_banner: A person or tool coming closer than permitted causes flashover across the air gap!
norm: PUE RK Table 1.1 • Safety Rules for electrical installations

title: Premises classified by electrical hazard
bullets: • Premises without increased danger: dry, normal temperature, insulating wooden floors, no conductive dust.
• Premises with increased danger: damp (humidity >75%), conductive dust, conductive floors (metal, concrete), temperature >35 °C.
• Especially dangerous premises: extreme damp (humidity near 100%), chemically aggressive environment or two signs of increased danger at once.
• Outdoor switchgear areas: always equated to the category of especially dangerous premises!
callout_text:
Any work outdoors
or in the open air
is automatically treated
as work in especially
dangerous conditions!
norm: PUE RK Section 1.1.13 • Electrical Installation Code

title: Touch voltage and step voltage
bullets: • Step voltage: the potential difference between two points on the ground one human step apart (0.8 m).
• Current spreading zone: occurs when an OHL wire falls to the ground or on an earth fault. Danger zone radius — 8 metres (indoors 4–5 m).
• Potential distribution: falls hyperbolically from the fault point outwards; the largest difference is near the fallen wire.
• No hopping on one foot: losing balance and falling onto your hands is deadly, as it creates a “hands — feet” current loop.
callout_text:
The danger radius
around a fallen wire
is 8 metres!
Never approach
a wire on the ground!
norm: PUE RK • Safe operation of electrical installations

title: 4 rules for leaving a step voltage zone
steps: Feet together

Immediately bring your feet
together so there is no
potential difference.
“Shuffle”

Move slowly, with the heel
of one foot against the toe
of the other, never lifting.
Step ≤ 10 cm
Get 8 m away

Keep moving until fully out
of the 8-metre danger radius
around the fallen wire.
bottom_banner: Never run or jump — losing your balance will be fatal!
norm: Safety instruction for emergency response in power networks

title: Section I summary: 5 electrical safety barriers
bullets: • 1. Hazard awareness: remember that current is invisible and never be careless in any operation on electrical installations.
• 2. Distance barrier: strictly keep the minimum permissible distances to live parts.
• 3. Environmental control: account for humidity, conductive floors and open structures, which cut body resistance tenfold.
• 4. Behavioural rules: no working alone where the rules require a crew or supervision.
• 5. Incident readiness: solid knowledge of step voltage and the first aid algorithm for a victim.
callout_text:
Electrical safety
is not a set of tips
but the law of survival
on an industrial
site!
norm: Section I summary • SafetyHUB

title: Technical safeguards
subtitle: Reliable earthing, insulation, extra-low voltage and electrical protective equipment form an impassable technical barrier.
norm: PUE RK Chapter 1.7 • GOST 12.1.019-2017

title: Protective earthing: how it works
bullets: • Definition: a deliberate electrical connection of the non-current-carrying metal parts of an installation to an earthing device.
• Purpose: to reduce touch voltage to a safe level when phase conductor insulation breaks down to a metal enclosure.
• Physical principle: the earth electrode resistance (Re <= 4 Ohm) and the human body (Rb ~ 1000 Ohm) in parallel.
• Result: most of the fault current flows to earth through the low-resistance earthing loop, protecting the person.
callout_text:
Current takes the path
of least resistance:
good earthing
takes the hit!
norm: PUE RK Section 1.7.51 • Electrical Installation Code

title: Earthing systems of power networks
bullets: • TN-S system: the neutral (N) and protective (PE) conductors are separate throughout the network — the safest system.
• TN-C-S system: N and PE functions are combined in one PEN conductor in the upstream part and split at the building entry.
• TN-C system: an outdated system with a combined PEN throughout; prohibited for new and reconstructed installations!
• TT and IT systems: TT — independent earthing of the installation; IT — isolated neutral with insulation monitoring (mines, mobile units).
callout_text:
Separating PE and N
conductors is the key
to correct RCD operation
and electrical safety!
norm: GOST 30331.1-2013 • Low-voltage installations

title: Protective neutral (TN): purpose and tripping
bullets: • TN connection: a deliberate electrical connection of exposed conductive parts to the solidly earthed neutral of the supply via the PE conductor.
• Protection principle: turns a phase-to-enclosure fault into a short circuit (SC) between the phase and the protective conductor.
• Protection tripping: the short-circuit overcurrent instantly trips the circuit breaker or blows the fuse link.
• Standard time: the faulty section of a 220/380 V network must be disconnected within 0.4 seconds (per the PUE).
callout_text:
TN connection turns
a fault into a short circuit
and cuts the faulty section
in a split second!
norm: PUE RK Table 1.7.1 • Automatic disconnection time

title: Residual current devices (RCD)
bullets: • Differential transformer: continuously compares the vector sum of currents entering the load via phase and returning via neutral.
• Leakage current: when a person touches a live part, a residual current (earth leakage) arises and induces an EMF in the secondary winding.
• Tripping threshold: to protect people against direct contact, RCDs with a rated residual current IΔn <= 30 mA are used.
• Response speed: a quality RCD disconnects the faulty circuit in 0.02–0.04 seconds, before heart fibrillation sets in.
callout_text:
A 30 mA RCD
is the only protection
that can save a life
in direct contact
with a bare wire!
norm: GOST IEC 61008-1-2020 • Residual current operated circuit breakers

title: Extra-low voltage (ELV / SELV)
bullets: • Definition: rated voltage not exceeding 50 V AC or 120 V DC between conductors or to earth.
• Application: supply of portable hand-held power tools and portable lamps in conditions of increased danger.
• Voltage levels: 42 V (or 36 V) — in premises with increased danger; 12 V — in especially dangerous conditions (inside boilers, tanks, wells).
• Power source: only via isolating step-down transformers with separate windings (autotransformers are prohibited!).
callout_text:
Inside metal tanks
and wells, only lamps
rated at no more
than 12 volts
may be used!
norm: PUE RK Section 1.7.53 • Protection against direct contact

title: Electrical protective equipment types
bullets: • Basic up to 1000 V: dielectric gloves, tools with insulated handles, voltage indicators, clamp meters.
• Additional up to 1000 V: dielectric overshoes, dielectric mats, insulating stands and covers, protective barriers.
• Basic above 1000 V: insulating rods of all types, insulating tongs, voltage indicators above 1000 V.
• Additional above 1000 V: dielectric boots, dielectric gloves (above 1 kV they are only additional!), mats.
callout_text: Basic PPE withstands the operating voltage; additional PPE is used only together with basic PPE!
norm: Instruction on using and testing protective equipment

title: Electrical protective equipment: 4 checks
steps: Test stamp

Check the next test date
on the stamp.
Expired PPE is prohibited!
Visual check

Make sure there are no cracks,
punctures, tears, chips
or mechanical defects.
Roll test

Roll the glove towards
the fingers to check for
punctures under air pressure.
Clean and dry

Before work, wipe off dust,
dirt, oil and moisture with
a clean, dry cloth.
bottom_banner: Using electrical protective equipment with an expired test stamp is strictly prohibited!
norm: SO 153-34.03.603-2003 • Rules for protective equipment

title: 4 steps to verify absence of voltage
steps: Self-check

Check that the indicator works
on parts known to be live
or with a test device.
Phase by phase

Verify there is no voltage
between each phase and earth,
then between all phases.
Induced voltage

Make sure there is no dangerous
induced voltage from adjacent
energised lines and phases.
Re-test

Re-check the indicator
on a known live source to rule
out a sudden failure.
bottom_banner: Always wear dielectric gloves when verifying absence of voltage!
norm: Safety Rules for electrical installations • Technical measures

title: Portable protective earthing
bullets: • Purpose: protect workers from voltage applied in error by switching devices and from induced voltage.
• Fitting order: FIRST connect the earth clamp to the earthing device (loop), and only THEN to the live parts.
• Removal order: strictly in reverse: FIRST take the clamps off the live parts, and only THEN detach the clamp from the earth electrode.
• Earthing conductor cross-section: flexible copper wires of at least 16 mm² (up to 1000 V) and at least 25 mm² (above 1000 V) for thermal withstand.
callout_text:
Fitting earths:
first to Earth, then to Phase!
Removing:
first from Phase, then Earth!
Wrong order is deadly!
norm: Safety Rules Section 3.3 • Fitting portable earths

title: Electrical safety signs and posters
bullets: • Prohibition: “DO NOT SWITCH ON! PEOPLE AT WORK”, “DO NOT OPEN! PEOPLE AT WORK” — hung on the drives of switching devices.
• Warning: “STOP! HIGH VOLTAGE”, “DO NOT CLIMB! DANGER OF DEATH”, “CAUTION! ELECTRICAL HAZARD” — mark off the danger zone.
• Mandatory: “WORK HERE”, “CLIMB HERE” — clearly mark the prepared and verified safe workplace.
• Indicative: “EARTHED” — hung on device keys and control handles and on earthed sections of the installation.
callout_text:
The “DO NOT SWITCH ON” sign
has the legal force
of an order! Only the person
who hung it
may remove it!
norm: GOST 12.4.026-2015 • Signal colours and safety signs

title: CRITICAL BAN: Breaching technical measures
bullets: • Do not start work in an electrical installation without completing all 5 mandatory technical measures to prepare the site.
• Do not switch on disconnected devices or remove prohibition signs and mechanical locks without authorisation.
• Do not use random wires of non-standard cross-section or twisted wires as portable protective earths.
• Do not touch live parts without verifying absence of voltage with a working indicator while wearing dielectric gloves.
bottom_banner: De-energising without earthing does not guarantee safety — induced voltage kills just like operating voltage!
norm: Safety Rules for electrical installations • Golden safety rules

title: Work organisation and permits
subtitle: Clearly divided responsibility, strict admission rules and the work permit rule out the human factor and errors.
norm: Safety Rules of the RK • Safety Rules • Admission to work

title: Two ways to authorise electrical work
left_card_bullets: • A written order on a prescribed form.
• Sets the exact place and the start and end times of work.
• Records the crew, responsible persons and safety measures.
• Required for de-energised work and work near live parts.
• Maximum validity — no more than 15 calendar days.
right_card_bullets: • A verbal task for a one-off simple job.
• Valid for one work shift of the crew.
• Must be recorded in the site operational log.
• Done by a small team (1–2 people) with a clear scope.
• Used for unplanned urgent minor work up to 1 kV.
bottom_banner: Routine operational work follows a pre-approved list, without a work permit or work order.
norm: Safety Rules Section 2 • Organisational measures

title: Electrical safety qualification groups
bullets: • Group I: non-electrical staff (office, warehouses, PC operators); briefing once a year, recorded in the log.
• Group II: electrotechnological staff (welders, crane operators, machine operators); 72+ hours of training, knows installations up to 1 kV.
• Group III: electrical staff; 1–3 months' experience in Group II, may inspect alone and work up to 1 kV.
• Group IV: may work in installations above 1 kV and act as work supervisor, permit issuer or person in charge of electrical facilities up to 1 kV.
• Group V: highest level (engineers, energy managers, persons in charge of installations above 1 kV); knows all circuits and rules.
callout_text:
A safety group
is a personal measure
of responsibility and
the right to independent
access to hazardous work!
norm: Technical Operation and Safety Rules for consumers • Annex 1

title: Persons responsible for safe work
bullets: • Permit issuer (work order giver): decides if work is needed, its safe scope and the qualifications of the crew's responsible persons.
• Responsible work manager (RWM): ensures the planned safety measures are complete and sufficient and coordinates the crews.
• Permitting officer: responsible for correct workplace preparation, checking absence of voltage, fitting earths and signs.
• Work supervisor (WS): responsible for a clear on-site crew briefing, correct use of PPE and continuous supervision.
• Observer and crew members: the observer supervises non-electrical staff; crew members strictly follow the WS's instructions.
callout_text:
Each responsible
person answers for their
part of preparation —
combining roles is strictly
regulated by the SR!
norm: Safety Rules Section 2.1 • Persons responsible for safety

title: 6 steps to prepare the workplace
bullets: • 1. Disconnection: make the required disconnections with a visible break in the circuit.
• 2. Locks and signs: lock the drives with LOTO locks and hang prohibition signs.
• 3. Voltage check: verify absence of voltage on all phases with a working indicator.
• 4. Earthing: close the fixed earthing switches or apply portable earths.
• 5. Indicative signs: hang “EARTHED” signs on device keys and handles.
• 6. Fencing: fence off the workplace with portable screens and hang safety signs.
callout_text:
Strict order of
the 6 preparation steps:
disconnect → lock →
sign → test →
earth → fence!
norm: Safety Rules Section 3 • Technical measures

title: LOTO protective lockout in power networks
bullets: • LOTO concept (Lockout / Tagout): mechanical isolation of hazardous energy sources with personal padlocks and warning tags.
• Personal lock: each crew member puts their own lock on the breaker or switch lockout device and keeps the only key.
• Group lockout: with several crews, a group lock box is used: equipment keys go inside, and every team puts its lock on the box.
• Error-proofing: no breaker can be switched on remotely or manually until the last worker removes their personal lock.
callout_text:
One worker —
one lock — one key!
No one can energise
the line while you
are working on it!
norm: International standard OSHA 1910.147 • Corporate LOTO procedure

title: 4 steps to admit a crew under a work permit
steps: Staff check

Check the crew by names,
ID certificates and electrical
safety groups.
Show on site

Prove absence of voltage,
show the earths, boundaries
and adjacent equipment.
Task briefing

Explain the work method,
danger zones, escape routes
and safe work practices.
Sign the permit

Permitting officer,
work supervisor and crew
sign the permit in person.
bottom_banner: No work may start without the permitting officer's and work supervisor's signatures on the permit!
norm: Safety Rules Section 2.7 • Crew admission procedure

title: Continuous supervision during work
bullets: • Duty of the work supervisor (observer): continuously supervise all crew members throughout the task.
• No leaving: the work supervisor must not combine supervision with any other work or leave the workplace.
• Supervisor's temporary absence: if the work supervisor has to leave, the entire crew must be withdrawn from the installation.
• Crew members: may not stay in the switchgear or at height without the work supervisor; switchgear doors are locked during breaks.
callout_text:
The work supervisor is
the crew's “safety eyes”:
doing their own work
means losing control
over people!
norm: Safety Rules Section 2.8 • Work supervision

title: Breaks and completion of work
bullets: • Lunch break: the crew leaves the work zone; the permit stays with the work supervisor; signs, earths and barriers stay in place.
• Re-admission after a break: the work supervisor personally checks that the workplace is unchanged and admits the crew without the permitting officer.
• Daily end of work: the workplace is tidied up and the permit is handed to the duty operating staff, marked as end of shift.
• Final completion: temporary fixtures are dismantled, crew earths removed, and the permit is closed with WS and permitting officer signatures.
callout_text:
After the shift, switching on
the installation before
the work permit is formally
closed is strictly
prohibited!
norm: Safety Rules Section 2.9 • End of work, workplace handover

title: 4 work supervisor actions during a break
steps: Withdraw crew

Stop the tasks, collect all
tools and lead people out
of the electrical installation.
Lock access

Lock the switchroom doors,
barriers and gates
of the work zone.
Keep the setup

Leave all signs, LOTO locks
and portable protective
earths in place.
Check before re-entry

Before resuming, personally
confirm the setup is safe
and the earths are intact.
bottom_banner: Crew members must not enter the work zone before the work supervisor returns!
norm: Safety Rules Section 2.9.2 • Breaks during the working day

title: Admission of seconded staff and contractors
bullets: • Secondment letter: the employer sends an official letter listing the workers, their safety groups and the rights of responsible persons.
• Knowledge check: seconded staff receive induction and initial briefings on the client's electrical installation layout.
• Admission certificate: issued when a separate fenced work zone is allocated to the contractor on an operating site.
• Assigning the permitting officer: initial admission of seconded crews is always done only by the client's own operating staff.
callout_text:
A contractor on site
calls for extra attention:
initial admission is done
only by the owner company's
own staff!
norm: Safety Rules Section 12 • Admission of seconded staff

title: Section III summary: Organisational control chain
bullets: • Unbroken chain: safety is guaranteed only when every link works — permit, briefing, LOTO and supervision.
• Personal responsibility: each worker signs the work permit for their own and their colleagues' safety.
• Documenting changes: any change in the crew or work conditions requires the admission to be reissued at once.
• Life comes first: organisational rules are based on the analysis of hundreds of real incidents and are mandatory.
callout_text:
A work permit is not
a formality but a legal
document that protects
your life
and freedom!
norm: Section III summary • SafetyHUB

title: Work at height and steeplejack work
subtitle: Falls from height are the leading cause of fatal workplace injuries. The right choice of fall protection saves lives.
norm: Rules on occupational safety for work at height

title: Work at height defined: regulatory criteria
bullets: • Basic height criterion: work with a risk of falling from 1.3 m (under construction codes) or 1.8 m or more above the surface.
• Guarding: work on platforms within 2 m of unguarded drops over 1.3 m, or where guardrails are lower than 1.1 m.
• Hazards below: work less than 1.3 m above machines, mechanisms, protruding objects, water or molten metal.
• High-level (steeplejack) work: work more than 5 m above the ground or a floor slab, done from erection fixtures or directly from structures.
callout_text:
Even an unprotected fall
from just 1.8 metres
in 85% of cases leads
to disability
or death!
norm: Safety rules for work at height • MHSD RK Order

title: Fall protection hierarchy: 4 levels
steps: Avoidance

Assemble units on
the ground before lifting
them by crane into position.
Collective guards

Install guardrails,
handrails, scaffolds, platforms
and safety catch nets.
Restraint

Use a restraint system that
physically prevents reaching
the edge of a drop.
Fall arrest

A fall arrest system with
a harness and energy absorber
to safely arrest a fall.
bottom_banner: Fall protection PPE is the last line of defence! Collective guards always come first!
norm: GOST EN 363-2014 • Personal fall protection equipment

title: Safety groups for work at height
bullets: • No group: work from scaffolds, platforms and towers with guardrails of 1.1 m or more, and from leaning ladders up to 5 m.
• Group 1: workers admitted to work as part of a crew or under the direct control of an appointed supervisor.
• Group 2: foremen, crew leaders, responsible performers and safety specialists who carry out periodic PPE inspections.
• Group 3: responsible work managers under permits, persons approving the WEP for work at height, certification board members, rescuers.
callout_text:
A Group 1 worker
may not work
alone — only
under the direct control
of a Group 2 or 3 specialist!
norm: Rules for work at height • Qualification requirements

title: Two protection systems: Restraint vs Fall arrest
left_card_bullets: • Goal: physically PREVENT access to the edge of a drop.
• Components: a work belt or harness + a fixed-length lanyard.
• No fall: the fall factor is zero (no dynamic shock load).
• Load: no energy absorber needed, as a fall is impossible.
• Limitation: never use where a fall into a void is possible!
right_card_bullets: • Goal: SAFELY ARREST a fall that has already begun.
• Components: full body harness + energy absorber + anchor line.
• Shock absorption: the absorber cuts the arrest force to <= 6 kN.
• Load distribution: the load is transferred to the thighs, pelvis and chest.
• Prerequisite: calculate the clearance below the worker.
bottom_banner: A work positioning belt (without shoulder and thigh straps) is PROHIBITED as a fall arrest system!
norm: GOST R EN 358 • GOST R EN 361 • Personal protective systems

title: Fall arrest system components: The ABC rule
bullets: • A (Anchor): a reliable anchor device (sling, clamp, beam clamp) with a strength of at least 22 kN (2.2 tonnes).
• B (Body wear): a full body harness with shoulder and thigh straps and a dorsal fall arrest D-ring.
• C (Connector): a lanyard with an energy absorber, a self-retracting lifeline (SRL) or a rope grab on a flexible line.
• 100% tie-off rule: when moving along structures, use a twin-leg (Y-shaped) lanyard — one leg is always clipped in!
callout_text: Fall protection PPE works only with correct anchorage and a calculated clearance!
norm: GOST R EN 362 • Carabiners and connectors • ABC rule

title: Fall factor and clearance
bullets: • Fall factor = Fall height / Lanyard length. It determines how hard the dynamic shock on the worker's body is in a fall.
• Factor 0 (anchor above head): the best option, minimal fall distance, gentle absorber deployment.
• Factor 1 (anchor at chest/shoulder level): a standard fall of the slack lanyard length; acceptable with an energy absorber.
• Factor 2 (anchor at foot level): CRITICAL risk! Free fall equals twice the lanyard length (up to 4 m); risk of hitting structures.
• Clearance: the calculated distance below the workplace (lanyard length + absorber extension 1.2 m + height 1.8 m + margin 1.0 m = 5.7–6.0 m).
callout_text:
Clip the lanyard
AS HIGH ABOVE YOUR HEAD
AS POSSIBLE! Factor 2 —
extreme load on
the anchor and spine!
norm: Guide to fall protection PPE • Clearance calculation

title: Anchor devices and rigid / flexible lines
bullets: • Class A: fixed structural anchor points on concrete and steel load-bearing building structures.
• Class B: portable temporary anchor devices (textile slings, tripods, I-beam clamps).
• Class C: flexible horizontal cable anchor lines for free, continuous movement of the worker along the structure.
• Class D: rigid horizontal rail anchor lines with a sliding trolley for heavy-duty use.
• Never anchor to unreliable supports: process pipelines, cable trays, radiators and window frames!
callout_text:
Never attach the lanyard
to process pipes
or cable trays —
only to verified
load-bearing structures!
norm: GOST EN 795-2014 • Anchor devices, requirements and testing

title: Ladders, stepladders and access platforms
bullets: • Three points of contact rule: when climbing up or down a ladder, always keep two hands and one foot (or two feet and one hand) on it.
• Leaning ladder angle: strictly 70–75 degrees to the horizontal (height-to-base ratio 4:1).
• Top end: a leaning ladder must extend at least 1.0 metre above the landing.
• Work ban: do not work from the top two steps of stepladders without handrails and guarded platforms.
• No heavy work: heavy erection and power electrical installation work must not be done from leaning ladders.
callout_text:
A leaning ladder
is a means of access,
not a workplace!
Heavy work is done only
from scaffolds and platforms!
norm: SNiP RK • Safe use of access platforms and scaffolds

title: 4 steps of a pre-use harness check
steps: Webbing

Check the webbing for cuts,
burns, abrasion and intact
contrast stitching.
Metal hardware
Fall indicator

Make sure the fabric fall
indicator is intact (the harness
has not arrested a fall).
Body fit

Adjust the thigh and shoulder
straps: a flat hand should fit
snugly under the thigh strap.
bottom_banner: A harness that has arrested a fall is immediately withdrawn from use and destroyed!
norm: Rules for periodic inspection and rejection of fall PPE

title: Risk matrix for erection work at height
rows: Person falling from height
Severe multiple trauma, spinal fractures, death
100% tie-off, Y-lanyard, horizontal anchor line
Falling objects and tools
Injury to personnel at ground level
Helmets, protective canopies, tool lanyards, 15 cm toe boards
Scaffold/platform instability
Collapse of the structure with people and materials
Anchoring to the facade, diagonal bracing, formal acceptance
Weather (wind, thunderstorm, ice)
Blown off by a gust, loss of balance, slipping, lightning strike
Monitor forecasts, stop work at once if wind >10–12 m/s
bottom_banner: The danger zone below work at height must be fenced off with warning tape and signs!
norm: SNiP 12-03-2001 • Occupational safety in construction

title: CRITICAL BAN: Violations during work at height
warning_title: STOP WORK AT HEIGHT IMMEDIATELY IN CASE OF:
bullets: • Being at height without a correctly worn and adjusted full body harness and a locked carabiner.
• Wind speed above 10–12 m/s (when erecting solid structures and panels) or 15 m/s for ordinary work.
• Onset of a thunderstorm, squall, fog (visibility under 50 m) or icing of structures and ladders.
• No approved work execution plan for work at height (WEP) or rescue and evacuation plan (REP).
• Using homemade, uncertified or damaged platforms, barrels or stands instead of scaffolding.
bottom_banner: An unprotected fall gives no second chance — safety at height is absolute!
norm: Rules for work at height • Stop-work conditions

title: Combined work, rescue and first aid
subtitle: Specifics of electrical work at height, preventing suspension trauma, emergency evacuation and first aid for victims.
norm: REP • Cross-industry first aid instruction

title: 4 safety steps for work on OHL poles
steps: Pole check

Check for wood rot or cracks
in reinforced concrete, pole
stability and guy wires.
100% tie-off

Use a flexible anchor line
or a pole strap
throughout the climb.
Safety zone

Keep safe clearances to
adjacent lines that are live
or carry induced voltage.
Earth the line

Fit portable earths
on both sides of the worksite
on all phase conductors.
bottom_banner: Climbing angle poles from the inside of the conductor angle is strictly prohibited!
norm: Safety Rules for OHL work • High-level work safety

title: Aerial work platforms (AWP) near OHL
bullets: • Work permit: work within 30 metres of the outermost OHL conductor is done only under a work permit and a manager's supervision.
• Chassis earthing: the AWP vehicle body must be earthed with a flexible copper conductor to a fixed earth electrode or the substation earth.
• 100% tie-off: an electrician in the basket must be clipped by the harness lanyard to the basket's dedicated certified anchor point.
• No travel: moving the AWP with people in the basket or with the boom raised is strictly prohibited!
callout_text:
Earthing the AWP body
and clipping into
the basket are mandatory
before switching on
the boom hydraulics!
norm: Rules for safe operation of lifts (aerial platforms)

title: 4 stages of the rescue plan (REP)
steps: Alarm and timer

Alert the supervisor at once
and start timing.
Rescue time — up to 10 minutes!
Rig rescue kit

Attach the rescue device
to a secure anchor above the victim
or on an adjacent structure.
Hook and lower

Clip the rescue line to
the suspended worker's harness,
cut their lanyard, lower gently.
Shock control

Place them in the right position
(sitting or semi-sitting!), call
an ambulance.
bottom_banner: The rescue and evacuation plan (REP) and rescue kit must be on site before work starts!
norm: GOST R EN 341 • Rescue devices and evacuation

title: Suspension trauma in a harness
bullets: • Injury mechanism: thigh straps compress the femoral veins and blood pools in the legs, causing acute venous congestion.
• Reduced blood return: after 5–10 minutes of motionless hanging, brain hypoxia, loss of consciousness and cardiac arrest follow.
• Self-help while suspended: if conscious, actively move the legs (“pedal a bicycle”) and stand in the foot-loop stirrups.
• GOLDEN RULE: after lowering, NEVER lay the victim flat on their back! (risk of “reflow syndrome” and cardiac arrest).
callout_text:
After lowering the victim,
NEVER, EVER
LAY THEM ON THEIR BACK!
Keep them semi-sitting
for 30+ minutes to spare
the heart from toxic shock!
norm: Medical emergency protocol for suspension trauma

title: Releasing a victim from current at height
bullets: • Step 1. De-energise the installation: switch off the nearest isolator, breaker or switch with the emergency stop.
• Step 2. Prevent a fall: remember that once the current is off, the victim will go limp and fall unless secured by fall protection!
• Step 3. Insulate the rescuer: if power cannot be cut quickly, use dielectric gloves, an insulating rod or an axe with a dry handle.
• Step 4. Separate the victim: pull the victim by dry clothing only, with one hand, without touching bare skin or metal.
callout_text:
When cutting the current
to a victim at height,
secure them from falling:
the fall after a shock
is deadlier than the current!
norm: Cross-industry first aid instruction • Electrical injuries

title: First aid: cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
bullets: • Assessment: check consciousness (call out, shake the shoulders) and breathing (the “listen — look — feel” rule for 10 seconds).
• Chest compressions: 30 presses on the centre of the breastbone, 5–6 cm deep, at 100–120 per minute with the heel of the hand.
• Rescue breaths: 2 mouth-to-mouth breaths through a barrier face shield after tilting the head back and pinching the nose.
• Using an AED (defibrillator): apply the automated defibrillator pads and follow the device's voice prompts.
• Fractures and bleeding: apply a pressure bandage to bleeding, splint fractures, do not reset bone fragments!
callout_text:
Start CPR immediately!
Every minute of delay
cuts the brain's chance
of survival by 10%!
Ratio: 30 to 2!
norm: Basic CPR algorithm (BLS) • MoH RK Order

title: CRITICAL STOP: 6 grounds for an absolute stop
warning_title: STOP ALL WORK IMMEDIATELY, NO EXCEPTIONS, IN CASE OF:
bullets: • 1. Sudden appearance of voltage on disconnected live parts or sparking at the worksite.
• 2. Worsening weather: onset of a thunderstorm, squall wind (>12 m/s), snowstorm or dense fog.
• 3. Detection of a defect or tear in the harness, lanyard, carabiner or anchor line during work.
• 4. Sudden illness of any crew member (dizziness, nausea, weakness, chest pain).
• 5. Forced departure of the work supervisor or the person providing continuous supervision.
• 6. An emergency, or tools or structures falling near people.
bottom_banner: The right to stop work (“STOP CARD”) is every worker's sacred right, with no risk of punishment!
norm: SafetyHUB golden rules • Zero risk tolerance policy

title: Final admission checklist: 6 safety conditions
checklist: Permit signed by all parties, still valid, task briefing given.
Switching devices off, absence of voltage verified, earths applied.
Personal mechanical locks on the drives, keys held by crew members.
Dielectric gloves, tools and indicators tested, stamps valid.
100% continuous tie-off, anchor point reliable (>=22 kN), twin-leg lanyard connected.
Evacuation kit on site, communications working, danger zone below fenced off.
norm: Final work readiness standard • SafetyHUB
